about: Production-build size budget per emitted chunk, in bytes of gzip level 9 output. Each chunk is judged by the first rule whose pattern matches its file name; a chunk no rule matches fails the check. Lowering a limit is free. Any other change to a rule (a raised limit or Stage 2 target, a new, removed, rematched or reordered rule) needs a new changelog entry naming that rule. See scripts/bundle-budget.mjs.

changelog.change: Stage 1 of #971, set once #968 made the release build the minified one. Measured at 101d0904: entry 243,072, dialog host 191,285, heatmap-3d 159,867 bytes gzip.

Stage 2 of #971, activated by #969. Every dialog is now its own lazy chunk, so the catch-all drops from 200,000 to its Stage 2 target of 60,000, and both Stage 2 targets are retired as met (three's already equalled its limit). No dialog needs a rule of its own. The irrigation dialog was expected to, but it is the largest at 45,626 bytes gzip. Measured on 8f1b4002 plus #969: irrigation-dialog 45,626, strain-library-dialog 39,706, label-templates 37,841, config-dialog 37,552, dialog host 9,231 bytes gzip.

#970 lowers the measured production entry from 244,100 to 193,300 bytes gzip after removing luxon, moving TC/label probes and optional graphs behind lazy chunks. The 170,000-byte target remains out of reach without a larger change to eagerly used chart/header code or the Zod classic schema style: Zod classic itself imports JSON-schema conversion and its mini flavor has a different schema API. Set the enforceable entry limit to 195,000 bytes from this build, and retire the unmet Stage 2 target.

#974 raises the entry from 195,000 to 200,000 bytes gzip for the irrigation safety chip, its detail and the Emergency Stop. Measured at 1b715d3c plus #974: entry 198,767 bytes gzip, 4.3 KB over dev, of which the chip and its detail are 2.1 KB and the safety slice, its localized labels and the tank card's hold note the rest. It stays in the entry on purpose: the lazy dialog chunks are what a stale HACS install loses first (ADR 0053), and an emergency stop that 404s with them is not one. A chip-only entry with a lazy detail would still exceed the 500 bytes of headroom 195,000 left.

GSM#668 raises the entry from 200,000 to 205,000 bytes gzip for the Active Grow Run chip in the header, its Start dialog, the grow-run slice and its localized labels. Measured at dev df785598: entry 199,162 bytes gzip; with the run chip 201,300, 2,138 bytes over dev and 1,300 over the old limit. The chip is part of the header the entry already renders, beside the safety chip. The remaining 3.7 KB is headroom for the rest of the Grow Run MVP's header surface (#669, #671); the Grow Run View itself (#675) belongs in a lazy chunk.

GSM#671 raises the entry from 205,000 to 206,000 bytes gzip for completing a Grow Run: the Complete run action and Live metrics line in the run chip's details, the lazy-chunk wiring that fetches the Run Completion Preview, the new refusal codes and the localized labels. Measured at dev 857dfbec, after #670 moved the Start dialog into its own chunk: entry 204,773 bytes gzip; with completion 205,671, 898 bytes over dev and 671 over the old limit. The dialog itself, its schemas and its two WebSocket calls are a lazy chunk of their own (runCompletionDialog, 3,570 bytes gzip), so what stays in the entry is the button, the chunk registration and the strings, which the card keeps in one eagerly bundled locale file. #668's reserved headroom was spent by #669.

GSM#673 raises the entry from 206,000 to 207,000 bytes gzip for finalizing a Grow Run. Measured at dev f758d2c2: entry 205,672 bytes gzip; with finalization 206,943, 1,271 bytes over dev and 943 over the old limit. About 480 bytes are the finalization dialog's localized labels, which live in the one eagerly bundled locale file; the rest is the Run Finalization Snapshot and Run Audit Entry schemas that get_grow_run's details now parse, the list_grow_runs read and its schema, and the header chip that offers finalizing a Completed Run, which has to be in the header because a Completed Run is otherwise unreachable once the Active Run Sensor reads none or names the next Run. The dialog, its preview and its command are a lazy chunk of their own (runFinalizationDialog, 3,500 bytes gzip).

GSM#917 raises the entry from 207,500 to 208,000 bytes gzip for correcting a Grow Run. Measured before #1034 merged, at dev 189244e2 after GSM#675's Grow Run View: entry 207,004 bytes gzip; with reopening and discarding 207,628, 624 bytes over that dev build and 128 over the current limit. About 410 bytes are the localized labels of the discard dialog, the reopen form and the View's two new actions, which live in the one eagerly bundled locale file; the rest is the run chip routing the View's discard and reopen requests, the discard dialog's lazy-chunk wiring, and the refusal reasons the shared Run refusal schema now parses. The buttons are the Grow Run View's (already lazy), the discard dialog and the two commands are lazy chunks of their own (runDiscardDialog and the correction slice), and reopening lives in the already-lazy finalization dialog.
Allow 128 gzip bytes for the four localized Finalized Run JSON export labels (GSM#683); export logic and schemas remain in the lazy Run view.

#1032 raises the entry limit from 208,128 to 208,500 gzip bytes for the probe_unresponsive and zone_migration_invalid safety labels, shared recovery advice and optional zone context. The safety chip and its details stay eager (ADR 0053); the Overview banner stays in the lazy irrigation dialog. Measured on b7fbac8c plus #1032: entry 208,334 gzip bytes versus 208,000 on dev, a 334-byte increase and 206 bytes over the previous limit.
